title: Breast Lift vs Breast Reduction: Which One, or Both?
meta_description: A lift raises breasts that have dropped; a reduction makes them smaller and lighter. How to tell which you need, when to do both, and cost and scars.
excerpt: A breast lift raises breasts that have dropped. A breast reduction makes them smaller and lighter, and raises them too. Here is how to tell which fits you, when the two go together, and how insurance, scars, recovery and price compare.
quick_answer:
Do I need a breast lift or a breast reduction?

It depends on whether you want to change your size. The American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) says a lift doesn't significantly change size, while a reduction removes skin and tissue, then reshapes and elevates the breast. A lift alone won't make breasts smaller, and women with both concerns may need a combination.

images.text_in_image:
Breast lift vs breast reduction

Breast lift
Goal: raise and reshape
Size: doesn't significantly change
Removed: excess skin
Surgery time: about 1 to 3 hours
Insurance: most plans don't cover it

Breast reduction
Goal: make smaller and lighter, and reshape
Size: smaller
Removed: excess breast tissue and skin
Surgery time: about 3 to 5 hours
Insurance: often covered if you meet your plan's criteria

Sources: ASPS, Cleveland Clinic, The Aesthetic Society
